"FC" <fcap...@hotmail.com> wrote in message news:<c6395m$kip$1...@news.net.uni-c.dk>...

Not grumpy, not at all! You are simply more demanding of quality
and thus, harder to please. I惴 like that as well. The new layouts and
backgrounds and constant changes are something that still hasn愒 been
explained clearly. To say that theese changes were made to make things
easier for the new players not only sounded odd, but you should see
the face new players make when I have to tell them that yes, not only
are there two different card backs, there are two different card
layouts as well, with slight variations to boot. And their racuous
laughter when I tried telling them once or twice that these changes
made things simpler for them... I even argunmented (against my
beleifs) that they didn愒 have to worry since all their new cards
would be from the same layout, but they always tell me it doesn愒 help
since they will play with people that have old cards, and will
probably want to trade for old cards or reprinted cards with the old
layout. So.... apart from wasting mine and my players time, and
getting some laughs out of people, ths argument serves no purpose.

If everyone were a bit more concerned about the quality of the
cards in general and more demanding of consistency and (I don愒 know
the exact best word for what I want to say in english)
aesthetics/visual quality/fine tuning/something like it... i惴 sure by
now we would AT LEAST have been given a reason as to why these changes
were made when they were made and/or been given previous notice/some
way to express our thoughts on such a big change.

I realize that there are people who could care less what the cards
looked like, but I do think that these people are the minority. I am
also not discussing purely subjective matters here (like artist X is
better than Z), what I am referring to are the background changes, the
new layout, the changes to the symbols, the way they couldn愒 even
place the disicpline symbols neatly on older sets like Final Nights
and Sabbat War (some were slightly off center, some slightly bigger or
smaller), the huge expansion symbols on the newer vampires (the most
useless piece of information on a card, especially on cards that have
the group number on them), the way each and every expansion has
printing errors, some are subtle like Power Structure not having the
Lasombra symbol in the first run of Sabbat War, some blatant mistakes
like the missing switched vampires from Black Hand, heck, even the
lack of imagination in creating expansion symbols from Sabbat War to
Anarchs (how much different can those ankhs get?) is something that
can be held against them. (how I miss the cool symbols from Dark
Sovereings and Ancient Hearts, and the different booster packs from AH
as well...)

I may be sounding a bit harsh, but we buy the game, and like all
card games, this is something completely superfulous (addictions
aside... hehe), which means that they need us. Not the other way
around. Many people, whether they realize it or not, sometimes seem to
be content with anything and act like we are doing WW a favor buying
this game so that they can continue to make it for us. These people
tend to get so frightened that mass dissatisfaction from players might
suddenly end the game that they get all riled up whenever someone
complains about these matters, any matters that aren愒 rules matters.
We need to abolish this "WW is an angel for giving us the game"
mentality and start asking for their best.

I am not saying they are giving us a bad game, or that they don愒
like what they do, but they could do it better. Note also that this
complaint has nothing to do with prize support, tournaments, leagues
or anything that goes in parrallel to the game itslef. WW has that
pretty well covered.

When a key Master card of yours gets Sudden Reversal-ed (or a location
Master gets Arsoned/otherwise blown up unexpectedly), you can now get
it back into your hand to play again, for instance. I can also see it
being used with corner-case Master cards. Example: putting a Fear of
Mekhet into your deck to deal with Arika-based decks, only to find
everybody playing weenies - now you can recycle it for something more
useful.

> - Siphon (do you often see vamps in torpor with blood on them?)

Every single time I see (or play) a Purge deck or an
intercept-Rotschreck deck or a Force of Will deck, for starters.

> - Black Hand Ritual (limited even for a black hand deck)

Likely true. But it's nice of them to show us that Events can actually
be removed from play.

> - The path of Lilith (why should I play that card instead of Fame?)

Try this: Why _wouldn't_ you play this _as well as_ Fame, assuming
your deck is an appropriate type of beatdown deck? Especially since a
number of players do put a Fame in their non-combat decks specifically
to contest Fames that might get played on them...

Also, I'd put this in my recent tourney deck _way_ before I'd put a
Fame in - it's an intercept-combat deck. I'd much rather know that
regardless of whichever vampire of my prey's I intercept, torporing
him will cost him pool, without me having to make a zero-stealth rush
(if I can get a rush, which my deck had, well, none of discounting
Beast) at the Famous vampire and have to struggle to even fight the
correct vampire.

> - Nightmare upon Nightmares (needs lot of Gehenna cards in play to be useful
> and Slaughter House already shown the power of discard in Jyhad)

Of course, Slaughterhouse has almost nothing to do with the 'power of
discard', except that they both make a player run out of deck faster.
(Slaughterhouse, since it burns cards off the top of the deck, does
not actually let or make anybody discard any part of their hand,
unlike NuN.) In any case, it remains to be seen how many Gehenna cards
will exist or how prevalent they'll be. NuN could be quite useful if
everybody's going to be using Gehenna cards.

Also, keep in mind that there's no limit to how many Gehenna cards a
specific player can play, aside from 'each only once'. (Assuming they
put enough in the set) a player could stack 4 or 5 event cards himself
to power NuN..

> - Crusade Berlin (cool artwork but beside that...)

As LSJ has stated, the artwork was a factor in making it a preview
card. *shrug*
>
> Jean-Philippe

-John Flournoy

Doesn't matter as far as whether you could block the rest of the actions
or not -- your opponent played it well to get your key vampire dead,
gone, and make you not a factor.

Of course, he's burning vamps backwards (as if he was your predator, you
could get a cross-table rescue), which isn't always the brightest
maneuver... but you can't legislate against questionable decisions. If
it really was a bad decision, you gotta blame the player, not the card.

Depending on how badly your key vamp was beating him up, it might've
been his only play to kill backwards that way, too.

>had three minions, and had to get out of torpor 3 times because of that damn
>card played by a Tzim intercept.

So you successfully got out of torpor three times, then? Sounds like it
slowed you down in that game, but didn't erase you -- and I'm sure at
least part of this was because he could only play it once per turn,
meaning all he could really do was stick you in torpor and use the
stay-tapped feature, not actually ruin your game.

I've never had trouble with people trying to use Rotschreck in large
numbers (more than 3)... mostly because I guess people realize that
piddling away your Master phase against your predator constantly really
makes it hard to win. Against your prey is a much better use, but you
KNOW your predator is going to pull the rescue, and now you have to go
reaching around with Eagle's Sight... *sigh* Just not gonna fly.

>So, you see, my incapacity to get vampires out wasn't a factor.

Actually, it was. Only three minions (one of whom is an obvious target)
is just not going to be enough these days -- you've got to be able to
get at least 4, with the threat of 5, or you either won't be around for
the endgame, or not a factor once you get there.

I don't think I've gotten a Game Win in the last year without at least
four minions showing on the table -- size irrelevant. And generally
I've had 5+ at the end of the game. Unless you can generate an action
advantage somehow, when it comes down to a headsup game, the guy with
more minions almost always wins.

Well, last gaming Wednesday I swept a table and collected 5
Rötschrecks in the process. ;)

I was playing Knights 2.0, my righteous Ventrue Antitribu
blocky-brawly, and in the mid-game period I got at least one Rötschrek
each round. My (2nd) prey was Tzimisce, and used Rötschreck, plus for
convenience had an Ivory Bow on Horatio (acquired from the time when I
was still wrestling with my previous prey, Goratrix' friends).

Knowing that momentum was my key asset (my guys were pretty rough,
meaning that even though I had no stealth to command, I could pretty
much get away with getting blocked, plus I had enough Forceds to be
able to risk completely tapping out every now and then), I went
forward relentlessly each round. I foolishly discarded my first TT
before the Tzimmie became my prey.

So, my typical turn was along the lines of: 1 bleed, 2 rescue attempts
blocked by prey, 1 blocked by predator, 1 succesful. (Yeah, I did have
5 minions, come to think of it...)

Of course, getting roughed up in combat was no problem for my guys.
However, my prey could not really play his Blood Dolls or other
masters. He was slowly dwindling away (partly) because he was using
Rötschreck and the game became a sort of stalemate. Rötschreck is
potent if it is timed well and you can back it up with some sort of
killah combo. Otherwise it is more of a frustration (but takes a high
toll on the methuselah who plays it).

Also note that you have more than one way to counter Rötschreck. You
can generally do it with Celerity, Auspex or Fortitude, and can reduce
its threat with stealth (Obfuscate or Obtenebration?) or if eventually
eaten, reclaim your guys with Necromancy. Meaning, pretty much every
clan has at least something to do with an effect that torporizes you.

Bye,

Daneel

I wouldn't say it's nothing. There are plenty of cards that either never see
play or don't see play in winning decks.

Having said that, I'm concerned with certain biases in statistics. One that
hardly ever gets mentioned when talking about winning decks has to do with the
frequency of play of one specific deck.

Let's say someone plays a deck once and wins with it. Fluke? Entirely
possible. But, let's compare to the situation where someone keeps playing a
particular deck/archetype until the player wins with it. In the absence of
other data to suggest that one deck is better, wouldn't the "1 for 1" be more
impressive than the "1 for 2+"?

Getting away from the frequency of play issue, as, this isn't the case with
Cameron and Slaughterhouse decks. But, couldn't it be the case that Cameron is
a superior player? Plays a particular style of deck that only works in his
hands? Etc.?

I guess what I'm getting at is that it's hard to make the argument to me that
something is good when there's a lack of back up in the form of other people's
success or in the form of "I played this a couple of times and had no problem
winning" or in the form of "after playing this, I see what you mean" (the last
is, of course, my issue and not someone else's but I only play so many games
and can't get to everything). I could see the possibility that the view is
correct and the argument is just the problem. I certainly form opinions based
on my own experiences that aren't widely held.
